summary: Navegador is a tight, efficient rondel-based economic game where players cycle through action spaces to build up colonies, ships, and factories while carefully managing an ever-tightening money supply. It rewards planning several rondel turns ahead and reading the sugar/gold/spice market, with privileges providing quiet but significant end-game scoring swings.
praised: Elegant, tight rondel mechanism with meaningful action-space tension
Clean, efficient design with almost no downtime or luck
Privileges add strategic depth and multiple viable paths to victory
Strong sense of economic engine-building and escalating snowball
criticised: Can feel dry or overly mechanical/abstract for its Age of Discovery theme
Slower player interaction is mostly indirect (space/market competition) rather than direct
Early leader advantages can snowball, reducing catch-up potential
Rondel plus privilege system has a learning curve that can feel fiddly at first

interaction.kind: Indirect competition for colony spots, market prices, and privilege slots rather than direct conflict

scoring.why: Final score combines privileges matched against colonies, factories, discoveries, shipyards, and churches, so the winner is whoever best aligns their privilege choices with their board presence
